title: Version is a hand-edited constant in Form1.cs — releases depend on remembering to bump it, and exe file properties show the wrong version
existing_state: The application version is `private const string ApplicationVersion = "0.51.23"` at Form1.cs:115 (the current git branch is literally named 0.51.23 — confirming a manual per-release edit ritual). It feeds the title bar (Form1.cs:329), the About dialog (6493), and the update checker (374-377), which compares it against GitHub release tag names via UpdateService.IsNewerVersion (Services/UpdateService.cs:35, 171, 727). SSH_Helper.csproj has no <Version> property and CI publishes pass none (build-release.yml:84-87), so the shipped exe's file properties report 1.0.0.0. The version therefore exists in two unlinked places (Form1 const + git tag); forgetting the const bump makes the in-app updater either re-offer the user's current version or fail to offer a real update — and nothing in the pipeline catches the mismatch.
recommendation: Single-source from the git tag: in build-release.yml derive `VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}` and publish with `-p:Version=$VERSION -p:InformationalVersion=$VERSION`. In Form1, replace the const with a static property that reads AssemblyInformationalVersionAttribute (falling back to a dev default like '0.0.0-dev' when unstamped). Optionally add a release-job sanity check that the tag parses semver. This also fixes the 1.0.0.0 file-properties issue that makes downloaded builds indistinguishable.
user_benefit: Update notifications become trustworthy (no stale-const window where users are told they're current when they're not), and support/triage can read the real version from the exe's file properties instead of asking the user to open the About dialog.

no <Version> property; only BuildTimestamp metadata is stamped
